claims.claim: Albemarle reported Q4 2025 Energy Storage volume growth of 17% and described improved lithium market conditions entering 2026, while preserving core Australian mining interests at Greenbushes and Wodgina.

The company idled the remaining Kemerton conversion train while retaining mining interests and alternative production channels, a weak signal that upstream resource quality remains strategic even as Western hard-rock conversion economics are being rationalized.

risks.risk: Lithium price volatility can overwhelm volume growth and impair conversion economics.
Idling Kemerton reduces Western conversion footprint and highlights cost disadvantages in part of the supply chain.

contradictions.contradiction: Lithium conditions improved, yet Kemerton economics remained insufficient to keep Train 1 operating.
contradictions.disposition: Preserve as evidence that commodity recovery alone does not guarantee downstream conversion profitability.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run restart economics and timing for Kemerton remain uncertain.

claims.claim: Full-year 2025 free cash flow was $692 million after capital expenditures fell 65% to $590 million, and cost/productivity improvements of about $450 million exceeded the initial $300-$400 million target.

At March 31, 2026 Albemarle reported about $2.7 billion of liquidity, $1.1 billion cash, $1.9 billion total debt and approximately 1.0x net debt to adjusted EBITDA after paying down $1.3 billion of debt in March.

risks.risk: Cash flow remains sensitive to lithium pricing and prior-period operating cash flow included a one-time customer prepayment.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong cost and balance-sheet execution coexists with ongoing asset rationalization caused by weak conversion economics.
contradictions.disposition: Treat as disciplined adaptation rather than resolve away.

unknowns.unknown: Full-year 2026 free cash flow depends on lithium price scenarios and is not a fixed outcome.
